history.quote: It started out as my typical "google and do the monkey-see-monkey-do" kind of programming, but then I cut out the middle-man -- me -- and just used Google Antigravity to do the audio sample visualizer.
As always, any JavaScript and style sheet stuff is all generated by antigravity. I lack both the competence and interest.

I've done all of the WebMIDI development using antigravity, because I obviously don't do JS (and let's be honest - I'm not exactly a UI person even in other languages, so let's not blame just JS here...). And today I decided to try Opus just to see how that works.

review_style.value: Opus writes verification scripts; the AI checks its own output
review_style.quote: And, incidentally, it also ends up being really useful to have the AI validate its own output. Win-win.

also.quote: This was all done with more of that "Let's just write verification scripts to track that it all acts the same" model of using an AI helper to change how I usually work.
And by "me" I obviously mean that I still don't really do python, so it's really just Opus.
you need to understand not just your prompts, but you need to understand your end result, because that's the only way you can maintain it long term

harness.value: Issue tracker on a separate git side branch, plus a hardware validation bench Opus drives
harness.quote: I copied over my issue tracking infrastructure that keeps track of things in a separate side branch, and the general rules, and hey presto - productive AI sessions with Opus.

rules_files.value: CLAUDE.md, not in the public tree
rules_files.quote: CLAUDE.md calls capture-rat.py the worked example for bench captures.

signature.caption: a bench that tests itself
signature.why: Our pick: he had Opus turn three pedals and a signal generator into an automated test bench, so agent changes get measured on real hardware instead of eyeballed on a scope.
signature.quote: I started the day with "I want to connect two pedals together and have them validate each other", and ended the day with three pedals, a signal generator, and a USB MIDI dongle all connected together as a validation bench with automated checks.

archetype.why: Has Opus build verification scripts and a self-testing pedal bench before he trusts a change.

signature_quote.value: I'm finding that I do things differently when developing with an AI than I do by hand
signature_quote.more: Having a test suite is no longer about writing the boring parts when Opus writes it for me, but instead about what those tests find.
